newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold demand seen slow ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold demand seen slow ahead of holidays.

text.p: South Korea's domestic gold demand was seen slow this week ahead of the summer vacation season which begins Saturday, bullion dealers said on Wednesday.
They said most South Korean bullion wholesalers' shops would be closed from August 1 until August 5 for the summer holiday.
"Domestic gold demand is slow this week due to the long summer holidays of local wholesalers," said a trader with Tong Yang Global.
The trader said the financial woes of the Kia and the Jinro groups would continue to depress domestic bullion demand.

Domestic gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal -- regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market -- was flat on Wednesday at 9,750 won per gram over the past week.
The company's silver price edged up to 140 won per gram from 139 won a week ago.

The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, rose on Wednesday to 895.20 won against the dollar from 897.00 won a week earlier. The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for bullion companies.
